To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tm is an essential component of the cooperative system, Tm-Tn complex is an allosteric system, the myosin head is the activating lig and the Tn-Ca2+ complex is the activator of the Tm-Tn system.

1) the thin filament is an allosteric system with Tm as the regulatory component, 2) Tn is an allosterically regulated activator, 3) the ATPase activity is mostly off in absence of myosins and 4) myosin heads shift the equilibrium from the closed to the open form, facilitated by the activator.

1) Tm and Tn are both essential for the cooperative/allosteri c regulation of actomyosin ATPase activity and 2) the Ca2+-dependent regulation of muscle contraction is a consequence of the Ca2+-induced cooperative activation of the thin filament.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of actin-myosin interactions and the mechanism of contraction.
understanding the mechanism(s) that regulate the thin filament and its interactions with the thick filament in muscle contraction.
understanding the molecular basis for Ca2+-dependent cooperative regulation of actomyosin ATPase and the role of the Tm-Tn complex in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tm-Tn-Ca2+ is the regulatory system that switches the muscle thin filament on and off in the absence or in the presence of myosin, respectively.
the muscle thin-filament is an allosteric regulatory system that operates in a classical MWC mode, with the myosin head as the catalytic site.
the muscle thin filaments are a classical allosteric system with Tn as the allosteric regulator and myosin as the catalytic component, and the thin filament is a classical MWC cooperative system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+ binding to TnC in the thin filament activates the ATPase by inducing the Tm-TnC complex to bind to actin.
the muscle thin filaments act as a MWC allosteric system with myosin acting as the ligand and Tm and Tn as the regulatory components.
the thin filament is the catalyst, myosin the activator, and Tm is the regulatory subunit of this system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Tm, Tn, myosin and the actin-myosin complex must all be included to explain the cooperative regulation of muscle contraction.
the thin filament operates as an allosteric system, and that the Ca2+ regulatory site on TnC is a true allosteric inhibitor of the Tm-actin-activated myosin ATPase activity.
the Tn complex, in the presence of myosin, can be considered as a true allosteric activator, and not just a Ca2+ switch.
